en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga,
Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Maidens (Kumāribhūtavagga), Discourse 76:
The Training Rule on Causing Dissension.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī approached the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs and requested permission to give the full admission.
Then the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, having deliberated upon the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī,
said, "Enough, noble lady, with giving you the full admission," and did not grant her permission to give the full admission.
The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī replied, “Very well.
Now at that time, the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs was granting formal authorization for other bhikkhunīs to give the full admission (vutthāpana).
The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī complained, grumbled, and became indignant:
“I am surely a fool, I am surely shameless, since the Saṅgha grants the authorization for ordaining other bhikkhunīs, yet it does not grant it to me.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant.

“How could it be that the noble lady Caṇḍakāḷī, having been told, ‘Enough, noble lady, with your ordination for now,’ and having replied, ‘Very well,’ would later fall into the state of criticizing [the Sangha]?

… “Is it true, monks, that the nun Caṇḍakāḷī, having been told, ‘Enough, noble lady, with your ordination for now,’ and having replied, ‘Very well,’ later falls into the state of criticizing [the Sangha]?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can this be, monks? How can the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī—”
‘Enough, noble lady, with your ordination,’ being thus addressed, she agrees, saying, ‘Very well,’ and afterwards falls into the state of criticizing [the Sangha].
This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...

And so, monks, let the nuns recite this training rule: “Whatever nun, having been told by a monk, ‘Enough, noble lady, with your ordination,’ should agree, saying ‘Very well,’ and afterwards fall into the state of criticizing [the Sangha], that nun is also to be dealt with according to the rule. And so, monks, let the nuns recite this training rule: [as above].

“Whatever nun, when being told, ‘Enough, venerable lady, with ordaining you for now,’ should consent by saying ‘Very well,’ and later fall into a state of reproach, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so on].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Enough, noble lady, with your having given the full admission."
“Enough, noble lady, with your ordination.
Having consented by saying, “Very well,” she later falls into a state of reproach; there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
There is no offense—
One who acts out of natural inclination, or through desire, hatred, delusion, or fear, is censured;
as is one who is insane,
and one who is a first-time offender.
The sixth training rule is finished.
